paper_metadata.title: Pattern-sensitive Epilepsy: Electroclinical Characteristics, Natural History, and Delineation of the Epileptic Syndrome

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the recruitment source (Mayo Clinic) and inclusion criteria over a 50-year span. However, as a tertiary referral center study, there is inherent selection bias toward more severe or refractory cases, and the participation rate of eligible non-participants is not fully transparent.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: 73 (43 female and 30 male) patients in whom pattern-sensitive epilepsy was diagnosed at Mayo Clinic (Rochester, Minnesota, U.S.A.) from 1950 through 1999.
items.reasoning: The authors clearly define the geographic and institutional source, as well as basic demographics (sex, age at onset).

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: nearly all patients undergoing EEG examination at Mayo Clinic who are capable of cooperating are asked to scan at least one standard pattern.
items.reasoning: While the screening process is described, the study relies on a clinical database from a single tertiary center, which may not represent the general population of epilepsy patients.

items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The remaining 73 patients included in the study exhibited epileptiform discharges in the scalp EEG during pattern viewing. ... Six patients were excluded from this study: three because of failure to elicit pattern sensitivity in the EEG laboratory, and three because of failure to give consent
items.reasoning: The criteria for inclusion (EEG confirmation) and reasons for exclusion are provided.

items.reasoning: While 73/79 participated, it is unclear how many eligible patients in the total Mayo population might have been missed or not screened over 50 years.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The mean age at onset of seizures was 12.6 ± 7.1 years... At presentation, 60 (82.2%) patients had exhibited one or more generalized tonic–clonic seizures.
items.reasoning: Table 1 and the text provide detailed baseline clinical and demographic data.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study achieved a long median follow-up (15.7 years), but 20.5% of the original sample (15/73) were lost to follow-up or had insufficient data for the primary outcome (remission). The characteristics of those lost to follow-up are not compared to those who remained.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis

items.evidence_snippet: Fifty-five patients were followed up for ≥5 years... Four patients were seen only once at Mayo Clinic, and neither they nor their relatives could be traced.
items.reasoning: 75% (55/73) were available for the 5-year remission analysis. This is acceptable for a 50-year retrospective study but introduces potential bias.
